rule: Typed receivers (decision A ...): a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). ... Body-less member declarations of scanned types are defined in the scan (high)
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type name) is method; new/super(...)/this(...) are constructor. Line 12: `local` is declared Shape (the declared type wins over the Circle initializer) and `param` is a Shape parameter; Shape#area is a body-less interface method of a scanned type, so high (Decisions 2026-11-09) and it must be in nodes (C1). 13-14: `var c = new Circle(..)` types c as Circle. 15: field `primary` declared Shape. 16: `holder.inner` is an obj.field chain whose property `inner` is declared Shape in Holder. 18: for-loop variable. 21: pattern binding `Circle k`. 26: catch parameter declared IOException (explicit import, outside the scan): the declared type names the ID even though printStackTrace is inherited from Throwable, medium. The enhanced for loop's hidden iterator()/hasNext()/next() are not written calls and are not among SPEC's implicit edges: no edge.
